posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I experimented with this and it it is really pretty easy. I don't know what the script would be for XP, but here is an example from MZ using Java Script.
if ($gameActors.actor(1).name().toLowerCase().includes("balls") ||
$gameActors.actor(1).name().toLowerCase().includes("") ||
$gameActors.actor(1).name().toLowerCase().includes("wimp")) {
$gameVariables.setValue(5, 2);
}
Essentially, you can add as many of these check lines as you want. For my experiment, I think I had close to 100. It was interesting trying to brainstorm content to exclude and it looks rather funny as one long script.
I am using a simple Variable value to determine if the name is ok or not. If the value is "2" like in the example above, whatever they typed in contains an unacceptable word or partial word. Otherwise the name is good to go.
Again, I don't know how this translates to whatever XP uses.
And I thought about this a bit too. Unless you advertise it to the player, many would never know that this sort of name check even exists.
Anyway, good luck!

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
I can see a system like this being really useful in a game intended for a younger audience--I can't imagine it would be a nice look if you made a game that was supposed to be for nine-year-olds and someone posted screenshots of their character with a name that is generally not considered appropriate for use around nine-year-olds XD Someone familiar with the idea of being able to name the characters in the game would know that that wasn't something that was strictly supposed to be in there, but someone who isn't familiar with that idea might get the wrong impression. Disallowing them seems like an erring-on-the-side-of-caution thing, to me.
(I'm aware most people here aren't developing games for nine-year-olds, but still--I was, at one point, so perhaps someone else is too.)

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
I feel like you are making the game to be exclusively played by your friends, and you expect them to do this just to bug you. In that case banning would be a great inside joke and the perfect premeditated revenge. You can even add a taunting message when they try a banned name. But I wouldn't do this in a public game, though.
As a random player, if this would happen to me before I got sucked into the game, I would already be done with it. Specially if I tried 2 or 3 names. Or what of a youtuber wants to stream your game, and their accountname is banned because it has a dirty word?
If it is a public game, then you can encourage your friends to use their real name or nickname. You could put special inside jokes in the game that no-one else would get, which only appear if actor 1 is named exactly the way you told your friend to name themselves.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
I know this might sound silly, but have you considered just not letting the player rename a character? Or you could give a list of names to choose from if you want to let them give some personality to their game.
I didn't do it for this reason, but one of my games gave the player a choice of one written character (letter, number, symbol, whatever). The main actor was a robot named something like TILOX- and the chosen character is added to the end. I mostly did it because I like being able to differentiate save files but it quickly became a cute feature the testplayers loved. You could adapt this idea to help prevent abuse.

module R2_Bad_Names
 
  BAD_NAMES = ["Word","Capital","lowercase",
              "friend","aa",
              "Badman","Other",
              # add whatever
              ]
  MESSAGE = "That is a completely unacceptable name to use"
end

# ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║                      End of editable region                        ║
# ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

#==============================================================================
# ** Window_BadName
#==============================================================================

class Window_BadName < Window_Selectable
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Object Initialization
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def initialize
    super(0, Graphics.height / 2, Graphics.width, fitting_height(2))
    self.hide
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Refresh
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def refresh
    contents.clear
    draw_text_ex(0, 0, R2_Bad_Names::MESSAGE)
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Handling Processing for OK and Cancel Etc.
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def process_handling
    return unless open? && active
    return process_cancel   if Input.trigger?(:B)
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Call OK Handler
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def call_okay_handler
    call_handler(:okay)
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Processing When Cancel Button Is Pressed
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def process_cancel
    call_okay_handler
  end
end

#==============================================================================
# ** Scene_Name
#==============================================================================

class Scene_Name < Scene_MenuBase
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Start Processing
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def start
    super
    @actor = $game_actors[@actor_id]
    @edit_window = Window_NameEdit.new(@actor, @max_char)
    @input_window = Window_NameInput.new(@edit_window)
    @input_window.set_handler(:ok, method(:on_input_ok))
    @message_box = Window_BadName.new
    @message_box.set_handler(:okay, method(:on_message_ok))
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Input [OK]
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def on_input_ok
    if name_good
      @actor.name = @edit_window.name
      return_scene
    else
      kill_name
    end
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Decide if Name is good
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def name_good
    name = @edit_window.name.downcase
    list = R2_Bad_Names::BAD_NAMES
    list.each do |nm|
      return false if nm.downcase == name
    end
    return true
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * prevent accepting name
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def kill_name
    @input_window.deactivate
    @message_box.show
    @message_box.activate
    @message_box.refresh
  end
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # * Message [OK]
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def on_message_ok
    @message_box.deactivate
    @message_box.hide
    @edit_window.restore_default
    @input_window.activate
  end
end

It needs a switch, because I got a better plan in mind, but I was able to replace:
Ruby:
def kill_name
    @input_window.deactivate
    @message_box.show
    @message_box.activate
    @message_box.refresh
  end
with:
Ruby:
def kill_name
    $game_switches[26] = true
    @actor.name = @edit_window.name
    return_scene
  end
and was able to trigger a Conditional Event that checks to see if Switch No. #0026 is ON right after Name Input.
I'll make sure to mark this thread as solved.
